name: OpenTelemetry
summary: Vendor-neutral CNCF standard and SDKs for collecting traces, metrics and logs.
use_cases: Instrumenting services once and sending telemetry to any backend; avoiding observability lock-in.
tradeoffs: It is instrumentation, not a backend: you still need storage and UI.
Maturity differs per language and signal.
avoid_if: you want a single turnkey product with UI and alerting included.

name: Sentry
summary: Error tracking and performance monitoring with stack traces, tracing and session replay.
use_cases: Catching and triaging production errors in web, mobile and backend apps.
tradeoffs: Self-hosted Sentry is a large multi-service deployment.
The Functional Source License is not OSI-approved.
avoid_if: you require an OSI-approved licence for self-hosting.

name: Grafana
summary: Open-source dashboards and alerting over many data sources (Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, SQL and more).
use_cases: Operational dashboards, alerting, combining metrics, logs and traces in one UI.
tradeoffs: Needs separate data stores for metrics, logs and traces.
AGPL obligations apply if you modify and distribute it.
avoid_if: you want error tracking with stack traces out of the box.

name: Prometheus
summary: CNCF metrics monitoring system with a time-series database, PromQL and alerting.
use_cases: Infrastructure and service metrics, Kubernetes monitoring, SLO alerting.
tradeoffs: Metrics only; logs and traces need other tools.
avoid_if: you mainly need application error tracking.

name: Datadog
summary: Managed observability platform covering infrastructure metrics, APM, logs, RUM and alerting.
use_cases: Teams that want one managed product for all telemetry with many integrations.
tradeoffs: Costs can grow quickly with hosts, log volume and custom metrics.
avoid_if: budget is tight or you must self-host telemetry.
